quotes.text:
* In general, there is little potential downside to nulling out the message
   *  database reference when it is in use.  As long as someone is holding onto
   *  a message header from the database, the database will be kept open, and
   *  therefore the database service will still have a reference to the db.
   *  When the folder goes to ask for the database again, the service will have
   *  it, and it will not need to be re-opened.
   *
   * Note: regrettably a unit test cannot verify that we did this; msgDatabase
   *  is a getter that will always try and load the message database!

source.basis: Quoted evidence supports the claim; its interpretation still needs current-source checks.

text: The retention test drops the folder database reference, forces garbage and cycle collection to release leftover headers, and then checks cachedDBForFolder. Only afterward does it use msgDatabase again to inspect counts. Follow that local observation boundary when testing closure. Clearing one reference is not proof the database is destroyed while headers still hold it. This is static source evidence. No runtime, build, lint or live accessibility check was run. Full Bugzilla and Phabricator discussion remains pending.
title: Test database closure without reopening it through the getter
